name: Scutellaria

project_scope.selection_mode: B041 canonical anchors + B153 strict-review handoff
project_scope.note: S. drummondii and S. wrightii are installed PASS anchors. S. ovata remains a true open strict-review task and is not installed.

study_strategy.warning: Do not identify skullcaps from blue-violet flower color alone. Start with life history and leaf architecture, then use hairiness and flower scale.

quick_key.if: small annual, acute leaves, visible glandular hairs, very short pedicels and small blue-violet corollas
low bushy perennial, rounded/obtuse entire leaves, minute pubescence, longer pedicels and larger corollas
much taller rhizomatous plant with larger triangular-ovate crenate leaves and very large corollas
quick_key.then: Scutellaria ovata — morphology comparison only until strict review is complete

look_here_first: FIRST find the SKULLCAP on a flower's CALYX: a small shieldlike projection (SCUTELLUM) rising from the upper calyx lip; it is not a petal. Photograph the flower from SIDE to show the projection and tubular two-lipped corolla. SECOND follow the flower stem down: an annual with acute leaves, short flower stalks and tiny corollas suggests S. drummondii; a compact bushy perennial with small round-ended entire leaves suggests S. wrightii; a much taller rhizomatous plant with broad scallop-edged triangular leaves suggests S. ovata. Check flower size with scale rather than blue-purple color.

look_for: Opposite leaves on typically four-angled stems
Two-lipped calyx with a conspicuous shieldlike SCUTELLUM projection on its upper surface
Four nutlets typical of the mint family, requiring mature reproductive material
shared_genus_pattern.glossary: SCUTELLUM = shieldlike raised appendage on upper calyx of skullcaps; CALYX = sepals surrounding base of flower; COROLLA = petals forming the colorful tube/lips; PEDICEL = stalk of one individual flower; CRENATE = rounded scalloped leaf teeth; RHIZOMATOUS = spreading by underground stems; PUBERULENT = covered with minute soft hairs; GLANDULAR HAIRS = hairs tipped with small secretory heads.
shared_genus_pattern.caution: The shield is a genus-recognition cue, not a species character by itself. A front-on flower photo often hides it; use a side view.

comparison_matrix.wrightii: low compact perennial, many stems, often 10–20 cm

comparison_matrix.drummondii: ovate, acute tips; lower leaves shallowly crenate, upper near-entire
comparison_matrix.wrightii: smaller ovate/elliptic leaves with rounded ends, margins usually entire
comparison_matrix.ovata: larger triangular-ovate leaves, often truncate to cordate bases, rounded crenate teeth
